attributes.body_ja:
「にて」は「に」と接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）「て」の組（く）み合（あ）わせですが、よく独立（どくりつ）した助詞（じょし）として扱（あつか）われます。「にて」は「で」と同（おな）じように「(A) の場所（ばしょ）で」「(A) の方法（ほうほう）で」「(A) の理由（りゆう）で」「(A) のときに」というような意味（いみ）を表（あら）します。これは「で」よりも形式的（けいしきてき）な表現（ひょうげん）です。

「にて」は主（おも）に、話（はな）し手（て）が強調（きょうちょう）したい手段（しゅだん）や方法（ほうほう）、時間（じかん）、場所（ばしょ）、理由（りゆう）、起点（きてん）を示（しめ）す名詞（めいし）の後（あと）に置（お）いて使（つか）われます。

これはフォーマルな表現（ひょうげん）なので、主（おも）に文書（ぶんしょ）やアナウンスなどでよく使（つか）われます。日常生活（にちじょうせいかつ）では「で」を使（つか）う方（ほう）が自然（しぜん）です。
attributes.body:
にて is often considered as its own stand-alone particle, despite originally being a mix of に, and the conjunction particle, て. When combined, にて becomes a formal case-marking particle that is used in the same way as で. This means that it can convey the meaning of 'with (A)', 'by (A)', 'at (A)', or 'using (A)'.

にて will primarily appear following nouns that illustrate a means, method, time, location, reason, or origin that the speaker wants to highlight.

As this grammar structure is formal, it will primarily be seen in writing, or heard in announcements. で will be the far more natural choice in casual conversation.

attributes.description: にて and をもって: Way of Carrying Something Out

attributes.body: に is a versatile particle marking direction, destination, the target of an action, or the place of existence. It commonly corresponds to English prepositions like 'to' or 'in,' and is frequently used in everyday conversation and writing. にて, however, is highly formal, appearing mainly in written documents or speeches, and is closer in meaning to で (indicating the place of action or means) rather than に (destination or existence).

Both are formal equivalents of で and can mark place of action, means, or method. において・における can also describe nouns, e.g. '現代社会における問題' ('problems in modern society') or '現代社会においての問題'. にて always connects to the rest of the sentence, not directly to a noun, e.g. '大会にて優勝する' ('win in the tournament').

first_relatable.title: において・における
first_relatable.meaning: In, On, At, Regarding, In terms of

attributes.body: で and にて both indicate the location or means of an action, differing mainly in formality. で is used commonly in everyday conversation and informal writing, whereas にて appears primarily in formal contexts such as business, academic documents, or speeches. Historically, で evolved from にて, with their sounds merging over time.
